title: Sales enablement playbook - positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook is the canonical Redwood Inference sales enablement reference for positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch-deck guidance, pricing recommendation heuristics, customer case study narratives, and the security FAQ used with prospects. It is intended for field sellers, solutions engineers, and partner reps.

Scope:
Covers value propositions for target buyer personas, concise competitive comparisons, recommended slide flows and talking points for meetings and demos, pricing guardrails and negotiation levers, anonymized case studies with measurable outcomes, and an FAQ addressing common security and compliance questions.

Target audience:
- Product and platform teams evaluating inference solutions
- SRE/Infrastructure buyers at companies running production LLMs
- Security and compliance teams evaluating private deployments
- Line-of-business owners evaluating cost/latency trade-offs

1) Positioning & messaging

Elevator pitch (30s):
Redwood Inference delivers predictable, high-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so engineering teams can ship reliable, cost-effective AI features without building complex serving infrastructure.

Top value props (short):
- Production-first performance: sub-second median tail latencies and throughput tuning with SLA options.
- Unified runtime: one API and tooling for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cost controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations drive measurable unit-cost reductions.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: automated routing and model fallbacks keep applications online during failures.

Buyer persona-specific messages:
- Engineering/ML engineer: "Ship reliable LLM features that behave predictably at scale — we give you observability, model versioning, and deployment policies so you don’t babysit token budgets or OOMs."
- Platform/Infra lead: "Centralize inference with reserved capacity and autoscaling policies that reduce fragmentation and improve utilization across teams."
- Security/Compliance: "Private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, and per-request audit logs for regulated workloads and data residency requirements."
- Product/PM: "Faster time-to-value with prebuilt integrations, evaluation harnesses, and rollouts for controlled launches."

Objection handling quick reference:
- "We already use cloud GPU endpoints": Redwood provides a unified serving runtime with batching, KV caching, and fallback model variants that typically reduce per-token cost and improve p99 latency compared to ad hoc endpoints.
- "Open-source models are cheaper": Running open models without operational tooling often creates hidden costs (ops, reliability incidents, and lower utilization). Redwood reduces those costs while letting you use curated open models.
- "We need on-prem for compliance": We support private/VPC and on-prem packaging with audit logging and KMS integrations.

Core proof points and metrics to cite:
- Typical customer throughput increase: +30-70% utilization after switching to Redwood Dedicated (customer-specific).
- Latency: median inference latencies as low as 40-120ms for short prompt generation on optimized runtimes (model & hardware dependent).
- Cost reduction levers: batching + KV caching + quantization can reduce per-token cost by 20–60% depending on workload.

2) Competitive briefs (concise)

Competitor summary table:
| Competitor | Positioning | Redwood strengths | Common weaknesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cloud vendor managed endpoints | Fully managed general-purpose inference | Higher throughput/latency tuning, model fallbacks, unified cross-environment tooling | Less integrated with self-hosted/private deployments |
| Inference runtime vendors | Focus on self-hosted performance | Unified hosted + dedicated + private offering, integrated observability and rollouts | Some vendors require building orchestration layer |
| LLM API providers | Simple APIs and hosted models | Transparent performance profiles, cost-control tooling, and private deployment options | May not expose hardware-level optimization choices |

Competitive talking points by competitor:
- Against cloud-managed endpoints: emphasize improved unit economics via caching/batching and predictable reserved capacity with SLA options.
- Against inference-only runtimes: emphasize Redwood’s hosted offering and turn-key private deployments (less ops work).
- Against LLM API incumbents: emphasize production-first controls (traceability, rollouts, per-route SLOs) and enterprise features (private deployments, KMS).

3) Pitch deck & meeting flow (recommended slide-by-slide)

Intro (1 slide): quick 30s company snapshot and trust indicators (customers, scale).
Problem (1 slide): reliability, cost, fragmentation of inference across teams.
What we do (1 slide): the Redwood promise — unified API, predictable performance, and deployment flexibility.
How it works (2 slides): serving runtime + smart routing + caching/batching (include simple architecture diagram).
Proof (2 slides): benchmarks (latency/cost), 2 anonymized case studies (metrics).
Security & compliance (1 slide): deployment options, audit logging, SOC2/ISO posture, KMS/HSM.
Pricing & contracting (1 slide): high-level tiers and enterprise options.
Demo or technical deep-dive (1–3 slides): live inference demo, SDK snippets, or deployment architecture specific to prospect.
Next steps & CTA (1 slide): POC scope options, evaluation timeline, and contacts.

Talking notes for SEs:
- Start with buyer’s top operational pain (e.g., "We can’t get stable latency under load").
- Use benchmark data tied to prospect-like workloads; always qualify model size and sequence length.
- Offer two fast paths: 1) Hosted API POC to validate latency/cost quickly, 2) Dedicated/Private proof for long-term isolation/SLA needs.

Slide assets (links): include links to the standard sales deck, technical appendix, ROI calculator, and benchmark artifacts.

4) Pricing guidance & negotiation levers

High-level pricing tiers (guidance; final contracts handled by commercial team):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation + per-embedding unit pricing; best for evaluation and early-stage customers.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commitment for predictable throughput and lower per-token economics.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + support + professional services for on-prem/VPC deployments.

Discount & negotiation guardrails:
1. Use committed monthly throughput/annual spend as the primary discount lever.
2. Offer short-term pilot credits for proof-of-concept but avoid multi-month unlimited credits without scope limits.
3. Discounts should be paired with minimum contract term for Dedicated or Private (typically 12 months).
4. Professional services scope should be priced separately and added to SOW.

When to recommend each tier:
- Recommend Hosted for quick trials and small teams (<100k tokens/day).
- Recommend Dedicated for sustained production traffic where predictability and isolation matter (typical threshold: sustained >200k tokens/day or p95 latency SLOs not met on hosted).
- Recommend Private for regulated workloads requiring customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM, or on-prem packaging.

Price objection playbook:
- If prospect cites cheaper per-token rate elsewhere: focus on total cost of ownership (engineering time, outages, inefficient utilization). Present a 6–12 month TCO example.
- If procurement pushes for heavy discounts: trade discounts for longer terms, higher commit, or expanded reference obligations.

5) Case studies (anonymized)

Case study: FinSolve (fintech, enterprise)
- Problem: High-volume document summarization pipeline with p99 latency spikes and high token costs.
- Solution: Migrated from ad-hoc cloud endpoints to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching and a quantized model profile.
- Outcome: 45% reduction in per-token cost, 3x improvement in throughput, and p99 latency reduced from 2.4s to 420ms.
- Quote: "Redwood gave us predictable SLAs and halved our ops effort for inference." — Head of Platform, FinSolve

Case study: HealthScale (healthcare SaaS)
- Problem: Data residency and audit requirements; initial experiments on public endpoints violated compliance constraints.
- Solution: Private deployment in a customer VPC with KMS integration and audit log forwarding to their SIEM.
- Outcome: Achieved compliance posture for HIPAA-adjacent workflows, zero production incidents in first 9 months, and improved deploy velocity for model rollouts.

Template for quick reference: insert this 4-section template in outbound materials — Challenge, Approach, Outcome (metrics), Quote.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for common questions)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: For Hosted: customer data is processed and stored in region selected at onboarding; data residency controls are available for enterprise customers. For Private: data remains in customer-managed VPC/on-prem.

Q: How is data encrypted?
A: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest encryption uses AES-256. Customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM are supported for Private deployments and Enterprise contracts.

Q: Do you support SOC2 / ISO / third-party audits?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certification for our control plane. We coordinate enterprise audits and provide evidence packages under NDA.

Q: Can we run the platform on-prem?
A: Yes — we provide an on-prem package with the same runtime and control plane options, plus documentation for air-gapped installation and support via our Professional Services team.

Q: How do you handle access control and RBAC?
A: Role-based access controls are available in the Console. For Private deployments we integrate with enterprise identity providers (SAML/OIDC) and can map groups to roles.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities exist?
A: Per-request audit logs, model versioning traces, and admin activity logs are available and can be forwarded to customer SIEMs. Retention policies configurable per contract.

Q: How do you respond to incidents?
A: We operate an SRE rotation with a documented incident process. Enterprise customers get prioritized incident channels and SLA-backed response times as defined in their contract.

Q: How is customer code or prompt data isolated from other customers?
A: Isolation is provided through dedicated capacity pools for Dedicated customers and VPC/on-prem options for Private. Multi-tenant hosted deployments use strict logical isolation and network-level controls.

7) Outbound sequences & demo checklist

Recommended POC options (3 paths):
1) Quick latency/cost benchmark (2-week hosted POC): provide sample prompts, run benchmark harness, deliver report.
2) Dedicated pilot (30–90 days): reserved pool sized for pilot traffic with standard SLOs.
3) Private evaluation (controlled on-prem or VPC): validated by security team with a scoped SOW.

Demo checklist for SEs:
- Confirm target model sizes and sample prompt mix.
- Run pre-demo benchmark with estimated cost and latency.
- Prepare rollback/fallback story (how traffic will be routed if issues occur).
- Security artifacts available: SOC2 report, network diagrams, KMS integration guide.

8) Assets & kit (links for sellers)

Must-have assets:
- Enterprise pitch deck (technical + executive versions).
- ROI calculator (spreadsheet).
- Benchmark report templates and sample runs.
- Technical appendix (API examples, SDK snippets, deployment reference architectures).
- Security artifact pack (SOC2, ISO summaries, audit process doc).

Where to find assets: Sales Drive -> /sales/redwood-inference/enablement -> folder: decks, benchmarks, security, ROI. Always use the latest dated assets (see file update badges).

9) Ownership, review cadence, and next steps

Owner: Go-to-market enablement (Asha Patel) — steward for content and asset updates.
Review cadence: Quarterly reviews for messaging and pricing; immediate updates for any material changes to compliance posture or pricing.
How to request updates: Submit a PR to the enablement content tracker and notify Go-to-market owners.

Appendices
A. Quick objection scripts (short)
- "We are worried about vendor lock-in": Redwood supports model portability and can export model artifacts and prompts; customers can migrate workloads across Dedicated, Private, and Hosted modes.
- "We need a reference customer in our industry": Use the anonymized case studies above and coordinate with Customer Success for a warm intro where permitted.

B. Quick technical snippets (for SEs)

  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
  resp = client.generate(model="rw-opt-6.7b", prompt="Summarize customer support tickets")
